Class 2 · Chapter 4 of 9

Lines, shapes and solids

Count lines and shapes carefully, describe solids and finish a mirror picture.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Find number and picture rules. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can count lines and shapes.
  • I can describe a solid.
  • I can complete a reflected picture.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Sides and corners

A rectangle has 4 straight sides and 4 corners.

Touch each side once as you count. That way you never count one twice.

Screen 2 of 5

Shapes inside shapes

Look carefully. A small shape can sit inside a bigger one.

This big square is made of 4 small squares. Count them all: 4 small and 1 big is 5 squares.

Screen 3 of 5

Solids you can hold

A cube has 6 flat faces. A cuboid is a box shape. A cylinder is like a tin.

A cone has a pointed tip. A sphere is round like a ball.

Screen 4 of 5

Roll or slide?

A sphere rolls in every direction because it is curved all over.

A cube has flat faces, so it slides and stacks well.

Screen 5 of 5

Make a mirror picture

Fold along the mirror line. The two halves fit exactly.

Every shaded square on one side has a twin on the other side.

Words to know
side
A straight edge of a flat shape.
corner
The point where two sides meet.
solid
A shape you can hold, like a ball or a box.
mirror line
A line down the middle. Both halves match.

For parents

What your child learns

Shapes hide inside other shapes, so count carefully. A solid has corners, edges and faces. A cube has 8 corners, so 5 cubes have 40. Counting in a system helps find all of them.

A common slip

Children often count only the small shapes and miss bigger ones. Count by size: small first, then pairs, then the whole. Keep a tally.

5-minute home activity: Hidden triangles

  1. Draw a big triangle and split it with two lines.
  2. Count the small triangles.
  3. Count the larger triangles made from two or more parts.
  4. Add them all and recount in a different order.
